newsitem.title: UK: UK's Major doubts EMU criteria can be met in 1999.
newsitem.headline: UK's Major doubts EMU criteria can be met in 1999.

text.p: Prime Minister John Major said on Wednesday he doubted whether European nations could meet the economic criteria for entry into a European single currency in 1999 and if they could not, then the scheme should be delayed.
"We have very great doubts that those criteria are going to be met by 1999, very great doubts indeed," Major told a BBC interviewer.

Major added: "If they (the criteria) are not, and the way in which the economies are developing in some European countries suggest they will not be met, then not only would we not enter in 1999, we do not believe the scheme itself should proceed in 1999 and we will make that clear to our European partners,"

Major, trailing the opposition Labour party with two months to go to an election, has been battling to maintain cabinet unity over the single currency after some ministers appeared to take a more hostile line than allowed by agreed policy.
Government policy, cemented in January, is that Britain will keep its options open on entry but believes it highly unlikely that Britain will join when the scheme starts in 1999.

Major sought to reinforce this in the interview, saying there were advantages in a single currency, mainly for trade and low inflation. But he said the government would have to balance these with the disadvantages before deciding on entry.
